newsitem.title: ANGOLA: More Angolan villagers flee unrest in southwest.
newsitem.headline: More Angolan villagers flee unrest in southwest.

text.p: Some 200 Angolans fled their homes to the southwestern city of Cubal on Monday as unrest involving soldiers from the former rebel movement UNITA swept on, aid officials in the capital Luanda said.
They followed more than 1,500 villagers who fled over the weekend, most coming from the area of Yambala, bringing with them tales of villages being set on fire and local people killed and wounded.
"The people arriving say some had to leave family members behind, some of whom were dead or wounded," said Catherine Quillet of the charity Medecins sans Frontieres.
Another aid worker from a different organisation, who declined to be named, told Reuters they had received reports of deaths and of men being abducted.
"We understand that UNITA is responsible for this and that this is the largest action in the area in the last two years," he said.
A 1994 peace agreement between UNITA and the government has brought the southern African country the longest period of peace since civil war erupted at independence from Portugal in 1975.

The area around Yambala used to be controlled by UNITA but has recently come under the control of locally organised civil defence units who are supported by the government, according to aid workers and other officials there.
It has historically been one of Angola's most unstable areas.
Cubal, a 10-hour walk from Yambala and the town to which the villagers had fled, already hosts some 120,000 people displaced by the two-decade-long war.
